nodes.summary: For a subgraph-isomorphism instance $(n, E_G, m, E_H)$, the host graph is the graph of the edge list $E_G$ on $n$ vertices: the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E_G$.
nodes.title: Host graph of a subgraph-isomorphism instance

nodes.summary: The decision problem SUBGRAPH ISOMORPHISM accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of subgraph-isomorphism instances, to an instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: SUBGRAPH ISOMORPHISM as a decision problem

nodes.summary: A subgraph-isomorphism instance $(n, E_G, m, E_H)$ is feasible when there is an injective map $f : \{0, \dots, m - 1\} \to \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ such that for every $(u, v) \in E_H$ with $u < m$ and $v < m$, the vertices $f(u)$ and $f(v)$ are adjacent in the host graph of the instance.
nodes.title: Feasible subgraph-isomorphism instances

nodes.summary: A subgraph-isomorphism instance is a tuple $(n, E_G, m, E_H)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of host vertices), a list $E_G$ of pairs of natural numbers (the host edges), a natural number $m$ (the number of pattern vertices) and a list $E_H$ of pairs of natural numbers (the pattern edges).
nodes.title: Subgraph-isomorphism instances

nodes.summary: The decision problem SUBGRAPH ISOMORPHISM belongs to NP, and every decision problem $L$ in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to SUBGRAPH ISOMORPHISM.
nodes.title: SUBGRAPH ISOMORPHISM is NP-complete

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
